item.text:
**Assessment**  
Mixed, leaning negative. The strongest positive evidence is procedural: the Constitutional Court rejected the election challenges and Jokowi formally handed power over in October 2024. But the year’s main reporting also shows repeated concerns about bias, dynastic advantage, and attempts to reshape election rules for his family’s benefit. I did not find strong evidence that Jokowi genuinely embraced fully contestable elections under equal conditions.

**Accepted Claims**
- [Indonesia leader accused of bias, interference in presidential election](https://www.theprint.in/world/indonesia-leader-accused-of-bias-interference-in-presidential-election/1948656/) - Reuters, 2024-02-01. Claim: Jokowi faced mounting criticism for perceived political interference and lack of neutrality, including highly publicized appearances with frontrunner Prabowo while his son was on the ticket. This is negative evidence for genuine acceptance of contestable elections. IDs: 4B.1
- [Indonesia students protest alleged poll interference by Jokowi administration](https://theprint.in/world/indonesia-students-protest-alleged-poll-interference-by-jokowi-administration/1963424/) - Reuters via ThePrint, 2024-02-12. Claim: Students and activists protested what they saw as Jokowi’s abuse of power to sway voters for Prabowo. This supports a negative reading of election contestability. IDs: 4B.1, 3B.8
- [Indonesia court rejects election challenges, upholds Prabowo’s win](https://theprint.in/world/indonesia-court-rejects-election-challenges-upholds-prabowos-win/2051948/) - Reuters via ThePrint, 2024-04-22. Claim: The Constitutional Court said there was no evidence of systematic fraud or presidential meddling, though the case centered on allegations of state neutrality problems and nepotism. This is the best positive evidence that the election was formally contestable. IDs: 4B.1
- [Poll shows Jokowi's approval rating falls after protests, but still popular](https://www.thejakartapost.com/indonesia/2024/10/05/poll-shows-jokowis-approval-rating-falls-after-protests-but-still-popular) - Reuters via The Jakarta Post, 2024-10-05. Claim: Public dissatisfaction rose after allies tried to change election rules in August in a way that would have helped Jokowi’s youngest son; the move triggered protests and lowered Jokowi’s approval. This is negative evidence because it suggests elite manipulation of electoral rules rather than clean acceptance of contestability. IDs: 4B.1, 3B.8, 3B.9
- [A decade of Jokowi: Indonesia's democracy icon leaves illiberal legacy, critics say](https://www.theprint.in/world/analysis-a-decade-of-jokowi-indonesias-democracy-icon-leaves-illiberal-legacy-critics-say/2310394/) - Reuters via ThePrint, 2024-10-14. Claim: Reuters’ end-of-term analysis says Jokowi left patronage, dynastic politics, and weaker institutional integrity. This is broad negative evidence against a genuine commitment to free and fair contestability. IDs: 4B.1
- [AP News article on Jokowi’s final year](https://apnews.com/article/indonesia-election-joko-widodo-7a47cf5e0811bedb95914b4ba20199bf) - AP News, 2024-02-11. Claim: AP described Jokowi’s final year as mixed, with criticisms of political compromise and concerns about dynastic politics. This is indirect but consistent negative evidence. IDs: 4B.1
- [Farewell-Welcome Ceremony for Indonesia’s President from Jokowi to Prabowo Subianto](https://setkab.go.id/en/farewell-welcome-ceremony-for-indonesias-president-from-jokowi-to-prabowo-subianto/) - Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia, 2024-10-20. Claim: Jokowi formally transferred power to Prabowo on inauguration day. This is modest positive evidence that he accepted the formal electoral outcome and followed the constitutional transfer process. IDs: 4B.1

**Search Gap**
- I found no 2024 source where Jokowi clearly and explicitly affirmed that power must remain genuinely contestable under equal electoral conditions while also addressing the bias and dynasty concerns raised during the year.
- The record supports formal compliance with transfer of power, but not a clean affirmative case for principled acceptance of fully fair competition.
